correctness.rationale: Correct for β>0, integer a,c>=2, fixed real b,d,r, real e>1, integer γ>=1. For integer m>=2 and arbitrary real phase s, u={mu+s}_β has exactly m−1 fixed points since an interval of length integer m−1 contains exactly that number of integer lifts. For each periodic base z orbit, compose integer second fiber to y↦{c^n y+s_y}_β then integer first fiber to x↦{a^n x+s_x}_β, producing exactly (c^n−1)(a^n−1) distinct periodic triples. Integer e also gives e^n−1 base points and formal rational zeta. In scalar β=1, 1<e<2, 0<r<=2−e no fixed points; any two-cycle necessarily alternates digits 0 and1 and its only candidate has z0=(1−(e+1)r)/(e²−1), z1=(e−(e+1)r)/(e²−1). Half-open branch conditions yield strict L_e<r<=U_e and primitive 2-cycle count (a²−1)(c²−1), golden-ratio transition. Independent exact rational digit enumeration at 4 e values and multiple boundary shifts checked the inequalities. Counts are fixed forcing only, not stochastic noise.
